title: The Liber Mortis: insight
summary: The secrets in the works of Nagash would break weaker minds, but not your will or your thirst for knowledge.

title: The Liber Mortis: madness
summary: You have learned much from the works of Nagash, but the cursed words have wormed their way into your mind, bringing twisted visions of the future and horrid...

title: The Liber Mortis: death
summary: The secrets of the book were too much for you. The dark power bound in the writings of the Great Necromancer tore through your mind and left a withered husk....

title: A Tomb King experiments on his servants
summary: You are an ancient King of Nehekhara, and the power of the dead is already part of your very essence. Thousands of servants rise at your command, answering...

title: The experiments succeed
summary: Your servants have submitted to every experiment. In the orderly, repetitive fashion that is the hallmark of Nehekhara, you have made slow progress, and you...

title: The experiments fail
summary: Countless servants spent, countless days of study, and the secret of Nagash's necromancy still eludes you.

title: A vassal asks you about necromancy
summary: The undead liege helps freely (same faith family), asks the student to convert, offers the blood kiss (a vampire to a living human), or refuses.

title: Your liege asks you to convert
summary: will help you uncover the secrets of the dark arts, but only if you forsake your gods and bow to the unliving.

title: The vassal converted
summary: has accepted your terms and abandoned failed gods to follow you.

title: The vassal refused
summary: has refused your terms, clinging to failed gods rather than learn the secrets of eternal life.

title: Your liege helps freely
summary: has considered your request and agreed to help you, asking nothing in return.

title: Your liege offers the blood kiss
summary: will help you, but only if you first let give you the Blood Kiss. Your studies, assures you, will be far easier once you are an immortal like .

title: The blood kiss
summary: has accepted your offer and come to your chambers at night, bared throat, and received the Blood Kiss.

title: The vassal refused the kiss
summary: has stubbornly refused your gift, still too attached to fleeting life to see the wisdom of your offer.

title: Not worthy
summary: does not consider you worthy of ancient knowledge.

title: The necromancer's test
summary: It has been hard to work it all out with no school and no master, but you have done it. You are a necromancer. At your word, the dead walk and speak once more.

title: A necromancer offers to teach you
summary: Accepting means taking the master's faith. A Phoenix King or Malekith frowns on unauthorised elven tutoring. targeted decision).

title: The offer was refused
summary: has rejected your offer of power over death.

title: What to teach
summary: After twenty lessons the apprentice is tested.

title: A lesson in caution
summary: Learning is harder for the living, easier under an undead or powerful master.

title: A lesson in daring
summary: spends long hours teaching you why a necromancer must be bold. Harden yourself to the horrors you will witness, and never hesitate.

title: A lesson in focus
summary: spends long hours teaching you that a necromancer must stay calm and disciplined at all times, for the dead obey only an unwavering will.

title: The necromancer's test
summary: Also fired when the master dies (apprentice.8).

title: Your apprentice is a necromancer
summary: has exceeded your expectations. At will, the dead walk again. Your work is done.

title: Your child is a necromancer
summary: It seems your child has taken a dark path and mastered the art of necromancy.

title: Your apprentice failed
summary: has proved a failure. Despite your efforts, cannot master the dark arts.

title: Your child failed
summary: It seems your child tried to master the art of necromancy and failed.

title: A wandering mage
summary: On the five-year pulse a human duke or king of the north, of Chaos or of Araby, whose court has no mage and whose liege does not follow an Old World god, may be offered one by a wandering sorcerer, shaman, scholar or witch.

title: A Chaos sorcerer
summary: A Kurgan sorcerer of Tzeentch, Nurgle or Slaanesh offers his services.

title: A Norscan shaman
summary: A shaman has come to your lands and won some favour among the locals. The soothsayer would join your court and read the bones for you, for a meagre price.

title: A scholar from the deserts
summary: A mysterious visitor from the deserts has come to your court. He is, apparently, a famous scholar from a faraway land, versed in the arts of magic and the...

title: A travelling witch
summary: An Ice Witch, a wise woman, or an Ungol hag of the old northern gods settles at the court of a Kislevite ruler. Turning her away is unwise.

title: Born with the gift (hidden)
summary: Rolled once per character. A child of ordinary parents is rarely gifted, and then only weakly; Tzeentch's faithful and elves more often, Khorne's less. A child with the gift in his blood (a gifted or carrier parent, a magic bloodline, the Witchling Star) inherits it more often and more strongly, or carries it unseen; a sure bloodline never misses. High doom stirs the winds and makes strong gifts likelier. A character created as an adult shows his gift within a few years (gift.2).

title: The gift shows
summary: On coming of age the gifted feel the winds. Where it is safe they can be open about it; anyone can choose to hide it. A hidden gift may stay hidden, or the lord may see through it (gift.7). Clever, shy and paranoid youths hide it best; a sharp, suspicious or magically gifted lord sees through it most often.

title: The gift, openly
summary: The gift becomes plain to all (the magic potential trait); the lord hears of it (gift.4). Also fired for a new Asrai spellsinger's apprentice (spellsinger.4).

title: A gifted subject
summary: The lord hears of a subject's gift. If his court mage is free to teach, he may make the youth an apprentice (apprentice.10 or apprentice.30).

title: A secret kept
summary: An independent ruler hides his gift. A player may change his mind and show it after all.

title: Hidden from the lord
summary: The secret holds, for now. Living in fear can make a coward.

title: Found out
summary: The lord has seen through the secret and will decide what to do (gift.8).

title: The lord decides
summary: A lord of a witch-burning faith, where even the gift is unlawful, may burn the youth. In Araby a girl, in Kislev a boy, can be hollowed: cut off from the winds for good. Under Malekith a gifted boy may be the one the prophecy warns of, and is killed. Any lord may spare the youth, angering the zealous among his people unless the gift is lawful.

title: The court mage takes a pupil (hidden)
summary: Relay for gift.4, so that the apprenticeship starts with the pupil as FROM: a sorcerer of the Ruinous Powers teaches the Chaos way (apprentice.30), anyone else the common lessons (apprentice.10).

title: Exposed
summary: A mage living openly under a lord who would burn him is found out at last and dragged to the stake. Stronger mages draw more notice. His liege and kin, if players, hear of it (gift.11).

title: Burned as a witch
summary: has been burned at the stake for witchcraft.

title: The witch confronts you
summary: A man under a lord appeals to him (gift.21). An independent ruler can throw the witch out or into his dungeon, at a cost in piety. FROM).

title: The lord decides
summary: Burning takes a hard heart (zealous, cruel, paranoid, arbitrary, or no love for the accused); a lord who is not Kislevite finds mercy easier. witch.

title: Hollowed
summary: has ruled against you. The witch lays her cold hands on your head and tears something out of you that you never knew could be torn. The winds are gone. The...

title: Spared
summary: has ruled in your favour. The witch leaves, but she looks back once at the door, and you know you have not been forgotten.

title: Waves of unknown magic
summary: Your studies have been disturbed of late by waves of unfamiliar magic. You have followed them to their source: a woman at court who studies the arts in secret....

title: The scholar confronts you
summary: , a scholar of the court, has discovered your forbidden studies and come to confront you.

title: The lord decides
summary: scholar.

title: Burned
summary: has ruled against you. The scholar's men take you before dawn, and the fire is already lit.

title: Hollowed
summary: has ruled against you. The scholar binds you with words older than the city and cuts the winds out of you. Women were never meant to wield this knowledge, he...

title: Spared
summary: has ruled in your favour. The scholar will leave you alone, for now.

title: The law has changed (hidden)
summary: Notes whether magic gained or lost rights, and tells the ruler and the players among his lords (magiclaw.2).

title: The Magic Menace
summary: The ruler's own copy sets up the great revolt: in 12 days a powerful vassal who disagrees is asked to rise (magiclaw.3); after 100 days with no revolt the ruler has won (magiclaw.8).

title: Rise against the ruler?
summary: A vassal who disagrees with the change may raise a faction against the ruler, call the other lords to it (magiclaw.4) and go to war (magiclaw.5). If he does not disagree, another great vassal is asked.

title: Call to arms
summary: Zealots of the other side, and Chaos cultists who want the realm to bleed, join most readily.

title: To war!
summary: The revolt's leader breaks from the ruler and declares war; the ruler and the players among his vassals hear of it (magiclaw.6). The ruler is pinged so that rebel troops can join (magiclaw.14).

title: The revolt
summary: Several indignant vassals have banded together against the new magic law. They have taken up arms to overthrow their own and restore what they call the...

title: The ruler won the war
summary: The ruler's new law stands, and magic's first lawful days begin a bloodline. The gained/lost rights flags are cleared a month later (magiclaw.15), so every copy of the news keeps its text. ruler (fired from the revolt CBs).

title: Nobody rose (hidden)
summary: A hundred days have passed without a revolt: the law stands. The ruler and the players in his realm hear of it (magiclaw.9); the rights flags go a month later (magiclaw.15).

title: A New Day
summary: For all the outrage over 's decision that not one of vassals was willing to contest it by force of arms. The new magic law stands.

title: The dust settles (hidden)
summary: A month after the revolt is over, the ruler's gained/lost rights flags go, which closes the revolt factions until the next vote.

title: The faction's ultimatum
summary: A magic law faction demands one step its way: the anti-magic revolters want fewer rights, the pro-magic revolters more. Giving in changes the law and tells the faction (magiclaw.11 - 13); refusing means war, and a weak faction may draw rebel bands, a strong one loyalists for the ruler.

title: The ruler gave in (to a backer)
summary: leader.

title: The ruler gave in (to the other vassals)
summary: Under pressure from a powerful faction, has agreed to change the realm's magic law.

title: The ruler gave in (to the leader)
summary: Your disloyalty is shocking. Still, to spare the realm a civil war, I will make the change you demand.Signed,

title: Rebels flock to the banner (hidden)

title: Fifty years (hidden)
summary: Fifty years after magic first became lawful in the Old World, people grow used to it (the magic_legal_old_world_50_years flag softens hatred of magic). A ruler who allows magic, a player if possible, is told.

title: Magic is accepted
summary: It has been decades since magic was made lawful. A few fervent detractors still rage, but the common folk and the nobility alike are coming to accept what...

title: A mage wins a peasant revolt (hidden)
summary: A human Old World mage (not Bretonnian or Kislevite) who leads a peasant revolt to victory makes his new realm a haven for magic (magic_law_2), and the Old World hears of it (magiclaw.23).

title: A Magical Realm
summary: Interesting news of an uprising. A peasant rebellion would normally be beneath our notice, but its leader, , is a mage, and has declared new realm a haven for...

title: A new realm without a magic law (hidden)
summary: The game gives no default law to a vassal who becomes independent. Where the law may be more than 0, he gets law 2 once magic has been lawful for fifty years, a random 0 - 2 while it is new, and law 0 otherwise.

title: Battle mages at game start (hidden)
summary: Non-historical rulers and courtiers may start as battle mages.

title: A chance of a battle mage (hidden)
The court mage is gone
summary: Your court mage, , can no longer carry out duties.

title: Teaching sharpens the teacher (hidden)
summary: Each year a court mage, or a mage with an apprentice, gains magic experience.

title: Nomad heir keeps the faith
summary: When a nomadic ruler dies, an heir of another religion group takes the ruler's faith. A government flip between chaos_horde_government and nomadic_government crashes the game, so the heir must match.

title: Samur chapter needs a witch hunter
summary: The Samur witch hunter chapter is destroyed when it passes to someone who is not a witch hunter.

title: The Everqueen dies
summary: A dying Everqueen hands Avelorn to her living heir (aiclean.4).

title: The new Everqueen
summary: The heir becomes Everqueen, drops her placeholder court title and receives every title of the late Everqueen.

title: Crown lost
summary: Every two years an Everqueen without Avelorn or a Phoenix King without Ulthuan loses the trait.

title: Dwarf newborns look young
summary: Newborn dwarfs and Chaos Dwarfs that inherited an old-age portrait set get the young one.

title: Growing old
summary: Every five years a human, Skaven or halfling of 50, or a dwarf or Chaos Dwarf of 200 (lifespan_age_50_trigger), gets the old-age trait that matches their looks; women become infertile and men less fertile, once. Old dwarfs get the grey-bearded portraits. Elves, immortals, Chaos champions and ice witches do not age this way.

title: Vassal conversion demanded
summary: Fired by the demand-conversion decisions: passes the demand to the vassal (aiclean.9).

title: Vassal conversion carried out
summary: Runs the vanilla conversion event 39700 for the saved converted target.

title: Spell failed
summary: Notification that a spell fizzled: the caster loses 25 prestige. Fired by the magic decisions.

title: Woodwalking ends
summary: Removes the woodwalking trait when its timer runs out. Fired by the magic decisions.

title: Greenskin government reset
summary: A new greenskin title holder on the second greenskin government goes back to the normal one.

title: Master dies
summary: When a mage dies, their apprentices are freed.

title: Dwarf ranks at game start
summary: Gives starting dwarf men the rank that fits their age and skills: beardling under 75, then thunderer, quarreller, hammerer or warrior, and longbeard from 250. Cowards are flagged and never become warriors.

title: Special titles die with their holder
summary: The Red Dukedom, Drachenfels and the Sylvanian empire are destroyed when their holder dies.

title: The Akghan church goes on
summary: When the head of the Akghan church dies, a new human mage of his faith and culture is created to take over (aiclean.17). The Rector of Martek is replaced by university.31.

title: Titles pass to the successor
summary: The new mage receives every title of the dead holder.

title: Elven youth
summary: Elves at adolescence become elven maidens or scions, which keeps them from low-born marriages; aiclean.19 ends it about 45 years later.

title: Elven youth ends
summary: Between 45 and 65 elves lose the youth trait, gain 50 prestige and can marry.

title: Court cleansing
summary: Every ten years an AI ruler below king with five or more Skaven breeders or ten or more Khemri soldiers at court quietly loses all of them. The AI spawns too many of them.

title: Mining outpost taken
summary: After a siege of a trade post, checks a day later (aiclean.22) whether the mining outpost still stands.

title: Mining outpost gone
summary: Clears the mining outpost flag from a province that lost its trade post.

title: Crown law cooldown cleared
summary: A new holder of a crown law title clears the crown_law_change flag.

title: Dynasty bloodlines
summary: A newborn joins every always_transfer bloodline their parents own when they share the dynasty.

title: Places of power and the Mists of Albion
summary: At the start of a new game sets the active, corrupt and inactive places of power across the map and the Mists of Albion (unless the game rule turns them off). Runs once, for the host.

title: Women's titles need a woman
summary: A man holding a female-led title (Sisters of Sigmar, Frosthome Lodge and the like) abdicates to a newly created woman of his faith and culture: a priestess for theocracies, a soldier otherwise. His court follows her, and the Frosthome heir becomes an ice witch.

title: Slann are Mage-Priests
summary: Gives every Slann the Mage-Priest character title.

title: Corsair titles
summary: Atruhayid feudal rulers with a port capital get corsair titles by tier.

title: The Dragon Emperor
summary: Fired from Xen-Huong's character history: creates the Heavenly Court, grants the imperial baronies and the nickname the Heavenly Master.

title: Game start setup
summary: At the start of a new game: Skaven surface tunnels under the burrows, secret faiths for members of the Chaos and Atharti cults, and male holders of female-led titles vanish (aiclean.26 has already replaced them).

title: Race trait check
summary: Gives a character without a racial trait the right one. Fired at startup, on employer change and by most effects that create characters.

title: Wrong faith
summary: A character in a faith their culture or race cannot hold is moved to the right one (by culture, liege and region). Players of human culture choose instead (aiclean.33). Gives up after 50 tries and logs the character.

title: Choose your faith, page 1
summary: The ruler designer asks a human player for their faith: the four Chaos gods, the necromantic faiths, Chaos Undivided, or the next page.

title: Choose your faith, page 2
summary: The faiths open to the player's culture: Norscan, Old World, Amazonian, Nehekharan, Cathayan or southern gods.

title: Choose your god
summary: The gods of the group picked on the first two pages.

title: Choose your vampire bloodline, page 1
summary: A ruler-designed vampire picks a bloodline: von Carstein, Lahmian or Blood Dragon, or more.

title: Choose your vampire bloodline, page 2
summary: Strigoi, Necrarch or Jade, or more.

title: Choose your vampire bloodline, page 3
summary: Mahtmasi, or back.

title: Choose your magic power
summary: A ruler-designed mage picks a magic power from 1 to 4 and, if untrained, gets a lore; then picks a potential (aiclean.40) if they have none.

title: Choose your magic potential
summary: Magic potential 1 to 4.

title: A lore for the untrained
summary: A ruler-designed mage who still has no lore or school gets a random lore.

title: Immortal portrait fix
summary: At adulthood an immortal race waits a month (aiclean.43).

title: Immortal portrait fix applied
summary: Sets the immortal's apparent age.

title: The Red Duke's bloodline
summary: At game start removes the Red Duke's bloodline from anyone but him.

title: Burnt by the flames
summary: A failed walk through the Flames of Asuryan founds the burnt bloodline, unless the redeemed one is already active. Fired by asur.3 and asur.4.

title: Redeemed by the flames
summary: A descendant of the burnt passes through the flames unharmed and is crowned: 500 prestige, 1000 piety and the redeemed bloodline for the whole living dynasty. Fired by the Phoenix King crowning.

title: Wonder levies refilled
summary: On loading a single player game, levies of wonder provinces at peace are refilled.

title: Move the Bretonnian court
summary: A new independent King of Bretonnia may move the capital to one of their own dukedoms.

title: Move the Imperial capital
summary: A new independent Emperor may move the capital to one of their own provinces.

title: Move the capital of Ulthuan
summary: A new independent Phoenix King may move the capital to one of their own kingdoms.

title: Wonder stage named
summary: Names and describes a wonder when a stage is finished. Not fired yet: most wonder names are still missing (was wh_setup.101).

title: Wonder upgrade named
summary: Names and describes a wonder when an upgrade is finished. Not fired yet (was wh_setup.102).

title: The curse follows the ruler
summary: When a Mousillon county changes hands, every five years, and at startup: the holder gets or loses Cursed Mousillon on the Mousillon provinces they hold.

title: Startup: set the curse
summary: On startup the host runs mousillon.1 for the holders of the four counties.

title: The Red Pox returns
summary: Once a lifetime, a Mousillon lord finds the pox in the lower city. Shut the gates (mousillon.11 tells if it held), let it burn itself out (mousillon.12), or, for a master of the dead, let the dead rise.

title: Behind the gates
summary: Did the quarantine hold? Two times in three it did.

title: The pox burns out
summary: The pox has had its fill. A living lord who walked the streets may have caught it.

title: At Landuin's tomb
summary: A pilgrim (decision mousillon_landuin_pilgrimage) reaches the tomb. What answers depends on who kneels: a master of the dead faces the ghost (mousillon.23), the worthy are blessed (mousillon.21), the rest usually meet silence (mousillon.24), sometimes a curse (mousillon.22).

title: Landuin's blessing
summary: The worthy pilgrim sees the ghost raise his sword in salute.

title: Landuin turns away
summary: The unworthy pilgrim is shamed by the ghost and carries it home.

title: The ghost draws his sword
summary: A master of the dead at Landuin's tomb: the ghost rises to drive the thing out. Flee, or stand and fight.

title: Silence
summary: Nothing answers. The pilgrim goes home with the road behind them.

title: A cup of black iron
summary: Once a lifetime and only once a world: a beggar in Mousillon offers a cup of black iron that smells of blood. Drink (the Black Grail artifact, a dream in mousillon.31), refuse, or strike him down.

title: Dreams of the black cup
summary: The Black Grail speaks in its bearer's sleep. A living bearer may wake with a taste for flesh.

title: The last knight at the chapel
summary: Once a lifetime, the lord of Mousillon finds an old Grail Knight kneeling in the ruined Chapel of the Grail. Pay to reconsecrate it (mousillon.41 tells how it went), let him die there with honour, send him away, or, for a vampire, feed. old knight.

title: The chapel's fate
summary: The reconsecration took, two times in five. Otherwise the stones bled and the masons fled. The old knight dies either way, at peace or not. carries over from mousillon.40.

title: The Grismerie floods
summary: Once a lifetime the Grismerie goes under. Lead men into the water to pull out the drowning (a chance to meet the Dracoleech, mousillon.51), wait it out, or bind the drowned as servants.

title: The Dracoleech
summary: Something huge moves under the flood. Fight it, or get out of the water.

title: The bride in the garden
summary: Once a lifetime, a lord of Dras or a lord at court in Mousillon meets the ghost bride. Give her a courtier, wed her (unmarried only), call a priest (mousillon.61) or ignore her and be haunted.

title: The priest's work
summary: Half the time the bride is laid to rest. Otherwise she stays, and is angry.

title: The Mad Duke gives a feast
summary: Merovech (character flag mousillon_mad_duke, set in history) invites his vassals and a neighbour to dinner. Each guest gets mousillon.71.

title: An invitation from Merovech
summary: A guest at the Mad Duke's table, where the meat is not pork. Eat what is served, flee in the night, or poison the host (usually caught, mousillon.72; the host hears of it in mousillon.73).

title: Caught
summary: The poisoner is caught and dragged to the dungeons.

title: A poisoner at the table
summary: Merovech, a player, hears that a guest tried to poison him.

title: The Festival of the Damned
summary: Once a lifetime, the city takes to the streets in masks of the dead. Let it run (the taverns pay, the streets riot), crush it, or turn the mob on a rival at court (mousillon.81 tells the rival).

title: The mob at the door
summary: A rival hears who sent the mob to burn their house.

title: Mousillon under the dead
summary: The King of Bretonnia, living, sees Mousillon ruled by a vampire outside his realm. Once in fifty years at most he weighs a war (mousillon.91).

title: The Damned Duchy
summary: Call the knights of Bretonnia to retake Mousillon (claim and war on its vampire top liege, who hears of it in mousillon.92), or leave it to rot. Mousillon.

title: The knights are coming
summary: The vampire lord of Mousillon hears that Bretonnia has taken up the lance. A master of the dead can raise the duchy's dead to meet them.

title: The Black Knight rises
summary: Once a game, when the doom engine runs high or very high (the End Times are coming): the King's bastard Mallobaude appears in Mousillon with a pressed claim on Bretonnia. If a master of the dead holds Mousillon, Mallobaude goes to them (mousillon.103). Otherwise he raises a host of knights and Mousillon's dead and makes war for Mousillon. The King hears of his son (mousillon.101), the lord of Mousillon of the war (mousillon.102).

title: A son out of Mousillon
summary: The King hears that a black knight claims to be his son and his heir. Deny him, or admit that it might be so.

title: The Black Knight rides
summary: The living lord of Mousillon sees Mallobaude's host on the road.

title: The Black Knight kneels
summary: Mallobaude comes to the master of the dead who holds Mousillon and asks for an army. Back his claim (independent lords only), hand him to the King (mousillon.104), or drain him. event_target:mallo_king carry over from mousillon.100.

title: A gift from Mousillon
summary: The King receives his bastard in chains from the dead of Mousillon.

title: The Unliving offer their swords
summary: Once a lifetime, a herald from Mousillon comes to a necromantic lord at war. The Mousillonian Unliving (d_mousillonian_unliving) will march for gold: a host of dead men-at-arms that falls back into the earth when the war ends. Afterwards they can be hired like any company.

title: The touch of Chaos
summary: Every five years one character in five may face the winds of Chaos: one in five of those rolls the mutation toughness test, then may become a Chaos Spawn (mutate.2) or be forsaken by the gods (mutate.3). Higher Doom, the Chaos Wastes, warpstone, cursed Mousillon and the Geisterforst, magic and a Chaos faith make it likelier. Skaven, Kislevites, immortals and the Hollowed resist.

title: Chaos Spawn
summary: The mutations overwhelm the body and the character becomes a mindless Chaos Spawn. Also fired by the mutation table effects.

title: Forsaken
summary: The gods' gifts never came, only the voices: the character becomes Forsaken, loses any Chaos champion or chosen trait, and every friend, lover and spouse turns away.

title: A new mutation
summary: Notice that the mutation table has given the character a new mutation. Fired by mutation_toughness_test_effect.

title: The mind strains
summary: Something has strained the character's mind: seven times in ten (fewer for the clever, the magically strong and long-lived races; far fewer for lizardmen and greenskins) the lunatic_counter climbs by one and the lunacy trait follows it. Mutations make the strain worse.

title: Raving lunatic
summary: Notice: the lunatic_counter reached 20 and the character is now a raving lunatic. One in five finds an invisible friend. Fired by lunacy_counter_check_effect.

title: Maniac
summary: Notice: the lunatic_counter reached 10 and the character is now a maniac. Fired by lunacy_counter_check_effect.

title: Twitchy
summary: Notice: the lunatic_counter reached 5 and the character is now twitchy. Fired by lunacy_counter_check_effect.

title: Madness drifts
summary: Every five years a lunatic, or anyone whose counter has reached a stage, drifts: seven times in ten deeper into madness, three times in ten back towards sanity. Long-lived and hardy races mostly drift back, or they would all end up raving over the centuries. The counter is first synced to the trait so that treatments and vanilla events that add or cure lunacy are respected. Climbing a stage shows a notice; falling back is silent. Only characters whose counter has moved carry the lunacy_counter_active flag (set by lunacy_counter_check_effect); it is cleared once they are fully sane.

title: Serving a monster
summary: Every two years a vassal of a mutant liege, or of a maniac or raving liege, who is sane, unmutated and not of a Chaos or Skaven faith, comes to resent them. A mutant liege takes precedence over a mad one, and only faiths that frown on madness mind a mad liege.

title: The resentment fades
summary: Every two years a vassal holding mutate.10's resentment drops it if the liege is no longer a mutant or lunatic, or the vassal has become one, has turned to Chaos or the Horned Rat, or is incapable or trusting.

title: A mutant at court
summary: A witch hunter on a court hunt spots a courtier of their liege whose mutation shows (mutate_exposable_mutant_trigger) and confronts them (mutate.13). Order mission hunts use whunter.10 instead.

title: Discovered
summary: The witch hunter has seen the courtier's mutation. The mutant can beg the liege for mercy (mutate.14) or flee the court before the fires are lit.

title: The liege decides
summary: The mutant pleads innocence of Chaos. The liege can burn them, imprison them, or spare them (whunter.17-19). Burning or imprisoning upholds the hunter's accusation.

title: Exposed
summary: Every year a follower of an Old World faith whose mutations can no longer be hidden (major or massive; minor for the AI), who is not hiding and lacks the cunning (intrigue 12) to keep them covered, is seen and cut down by their own court. Players in the realm hear of a landed victim (mutate.16).

title: A lord cut down
summary: Players hear that a fellow lord of the realm was cut down by their own guards as a mutant. They can choose not to hear such news again.

title: A unit moves
summary: Hidden. Whenever a commander's unit enters a province: the Convoy Master may have reached the port (erengrad.13); at sea, the naval battle check runs (naval.100) and, once a year at most, one time in thirty-three a voyage event comes up. The Convoy Master at sea meets them three times as often.

title: Storm
summary: A storm falls on the fleet; worse in the Sea of Claws. Ride it out, pray to Manann, or run for the coast and lose time.

title: Man overboard
summary: A sailor goes over the side in a heavy sea. Go in after him, throw a line, or leave him to Manann.

title: Sickness aboard
summary: A fever runs through the crews. Put in at the nearest port and lose time, or press on and risk it.

title: Longships!
summary: Norscan raiders come out of the sea-mist. Fight, pay them off, or try to outrun them.

title: The Norscan toll
summary: A jarl's longships bar the strait and demand a toll. Pay, refuse (the raiders come, naval.11), or, if the commander's lord rules, swear a trade-friendship that opens a route north.

title: Something in the water
summary: A sea monster is sighted in the Sea of Claws. Hunt it (naval.13), or steer clear.

title: On its trail
summary: Days of following wreckage and blood in the water. Press on (naval.14), or give up the hunt.

title: The leviathan rises
summary: The monster turns on the hunters. Win (naval.15) or lose (naval.16).

title: The leviathan dies
summary: The hunters bring back its tooth: half the time the commander keeps one, once a lifetime.

title: The leviathan wins
summary: Ships are lost, the commander is hurt, and the beast swims free.

title: A pirate's offer
summary: A pirate captain offers to sail under the commander's lord's flag in return for amnesty. Accept (the top liege gets his ships; in some years the pirate may turn, naval.18), refuse, or hang him.

title: The pirate's choice
summary: Years later the pardoned pirate keeps faith (two times in three) or sails off with the ships and a hold full of the realm's silver.

title: Elven sails
summary: An Asur trading ship hails the fleet. Trade, or let an Elf mage take passage. The Erengrad Convoy Master can win an Ulthuan trade deal for Erengrad instead.

title: The White Star
summary: The Knights of the White Star, Ulric's knights of Erengrad, offer their warships as escort through the Sea of Claws. Raiders and tolls keep away for a year; the Orthodoxy of Ursun dislikes the favour to Ulric.

title: Hostile fleet nearby
summary: Hidden. An admiral at sea who shares a sea zone with a hostile fleet saves both sides and asks the attacker whether to engage (naval.101). Sea raiders (naval_sea_raider_trigger) treat every foreign admiral as fair game; everyone else only fleets they are at war with. Runs on every move at sea, so it bails out early: no war and no raider means no search, and both admirals get naval_battle_cd (60 days) once they have met.

title: Hostile admiral spotted (attacker)
summary: Engage (naval.102), raid a fleet you are not at war with, or let the defender decide (naval.104).

title: Naval battle (attacker)
summary: The attacker's outcome; the defending liege hears of it (naval.103).

title: News of a sea battle
summary: has decided to attack my detachment located in the .

title: Hostile admiral spotted (defender)
summary: Engage (naval.105) or slip away.

title: Naval battle (defender)
summary: The defender's outcome; the attacking liege hears of it (naval.103).

title: The Frost Fair
summary: In a hard winter the rivers of Kislev freeze and a fair grows on the ice. Walk the fair (one of oblast.2 - 5), or stay in the warm. The ice may crack under the crowd (oblast.6).

title: The race on the ice
summary: Horses race on the frozen river. Bet on the Ungol mare, on the Gospodar stallion, or keep your purse shut.

title: The bear pit
summary: Showmen have dug a pit in the ice and set dogs on a chained bear. The crowd loves it; the priests of Ursun do not.

title: The Praag jeweller
summary: A silversmith from Praag sells filigree on the ice. Buy a chain (once a lifetime, only for one without), or haggle and walk away.

title: The cutpurse
summary: A cutpurse caught with his hand in the lord's purse has a Chaos mark under his shirt. Hand him to the priests (piety), or have him followed to his masters (intrigue, and a cult broken or a scout lost).

title: The ice cracks
summary: The river ice gives way under the crowd. Go in after the drowning (a chance of a wound and great prestige), or watch from the bank and lose a courtier to the river.

title: The Long Ride
summary: Every ten years the Ungol tribes hold a great horse race across the steppe. Ride in it (oblast.11), stake a horse, place a bet, or watch.

title: The ride
summary: The race runs from dawn to dusk across the steppe. A win brings great prestige and, rarely, a famous steppe horse (once a lifetime, only for a rider without one). A Gospodar winner galls the Ungols. A bad fall brings a wound.

title: The cub
summary: Hunters bring in a bear cub whose mother they killed. Keep it (a cub that grows into a companion in five to eight years, oblast.21), give it to the priests of Ursun, or let the hunters have the pelt.

title: The cub is grown
summary: The cub is a full-grown bear that follows its master like a dog. Keep it as a companion (a trait), or, for a member of the Circle of the Bear, train it for war (the war bear mount). It dies of age in time (oblast.25).

title: The bear is sick
summary: The companion bear will not eat. Pay a Strigany animal healer, or leave it to Ursun (it may die, oblast.25).

title: The bear mauls a guest
summary: A guest teased the companion bear and lost half an arm. Pay the guest's family, or say he had it coming.

title: The bear and the assassin
summary: A knife in the dark, and the companion bear gets to the assassin first. Once a lifetime.

title: The old bear dies
summary: The companion bear dies of age or sickness, and its master grieves.

title: The drinking contest
summary: A rival or a boyar challenges the lord to drink him under the table. Accept (a contest of health and martial, oblast.31), or decline and be mocked.

title: Under the table
summary: Who falls first? A win brings a bet and, from a rival, sometimes a sworn friendship; a loss spills a secret or costs a wager. Rarely, the loser wakes to find he signed away a hunting lodge.

title: Blood feud
summary: Two of the lord's vassals have fallen into a blood feud over a stolen bride, a dead horse or an insult at the bear dance. Rule for one (his loyalty, the other's grudge), share the blame, or let them fight it out (oblast.41).

title: Burnt farms
summary: The feud that nobody stopped has burned half a district. The lord's capital county has more unrest for five years, and the two families hate each other.

title: A letter from the Legion
summary: Kin who ride with the Gryphon Legion in the Empire (kislev.50 - 55) write home of a battle, and send loot.

title: A southern wife
summary: The kin in the Legion writes that he has married an Imperial widow. Bless the match, or forbid it and anger him.

title: A debt in Nuln
summary: The kin in the Legion has run up a gambling debt in Nuln and begs for gold. Pay it, or let him find his own way out.

title: The Shrine falls to an outsider (hidden)
summary: The title flag stops a second demand while one is pending.

title: The silent demand
summary: A Phoenix Guard brings a written demand: leave the Isle of Flame. Yield, and the isle goes to the Phoenix King (or a warden of the shrine). Refuse, and the Guard rise in a religious revolt for the isle.

title: Praag falls
summary: Hidden. A servant of Chaos wins a siege of a Praag holding: the city has fallen. If the curse was eased, it comes back at once.

title: Praag changes hands
summary: Hidden. A servant of Chaos taking the county counts as the fall. A free ruler taking it after the fall brings down the curse (praag.3).

title: The Curse of Praag
summary: The city is free again, but what the Chaos sorcerers did to it does not leave. Faces in the walls, madness, and the richest craftsmen in Kislev.

title: The curse returns
summary: Hidden. Every five years: when the Duma's rebuilding has worn off, the curse comes back.

title: The city takes another mind
summary: A courtier who lives in cursed Praag begins to hear the walls. Send them to the Ice Witches for healing, or let it run its course.

title: A child of the walls
summary: A child is born with the mark of the curse on them. Hide them, send them to the Ice Witches, or give them to the Furnace.

title: Faces in the walls
summary: Agonised faces push out of the stones of the palace. Pray, wall them over, or listen to what they say (a secret, and a step towards madness).

title: The Furnace men
summary: The men who smash the risen dead at night ask for gold, oil and men. Help them (Ashes Not Graves on the city; rarely their hammer for the ruler), or send them away.

title: The dead walk in Praag
summary: A district wakes to find its dead walking. Likelier when the Furnace men were sent away. Lead the Furnace men yourself, pay the garrison, or close the district and let it burn.

title: The undertaker
summary: One of Praag's undertakers is found raising what he should be burning. Burn him, take him into service, or drive him out.

title: The silversmiths' street
summary: The jewellers of Praag offer a commission. Pay for a fine piece (one time in four, once a lifetime, a Praag filigree chain), or decline.

title: The Observatory
summary: An astronomer of the old Observatory has read the stars over Kislev. Fund the readings, or send him back to his tower.

title: The missing servants
summary: Servants of the great houses go missing in the night. Look into it (the hunt begins), or let it be.

title: Never at dawn prayers
summary: A boyar of the Duma never comes to the dawn prayers, and never to a daytime feast. Keep watching (praag.42), or drop it.

title: The portrait
summary: In the boyar's house hangs a portrait of his great-grandfather. It is the boyar, to the last grey hair. The truth comes out (praag.43).

title: The boyars who do not age
summary: The vampire boyars are found out: the Upirnovs (von Carstein blood) or the Kalashinivik sisters (Lahmians). Purge them with the Circle of the Bear, bargain for gold and secrets (one of them stays at court), or be drawn in as their living thrall.

title: The Upirnov captain
summary: A pale boyar of the Upirnovs offers to keep the peace in Praag's streets. He is very good at it. Take him into service (a hidden vampire at court, Praag quieter for twenty years), or decline.

title: A Vasilikov's claim
summary: A Vasilikov arrives with a chest of old charters: his house, he says, held a quarter of Praag before the Tzarina's time. Recognise the claim (he joins the court with a claim on a city of Praag), refuse him, or throw him in the cells.

title: An opera about the reign
summary: The Opera House offers to stage an opera about the ruler. Commission it (a triumph, or a scandal if the librettist mocks you), or decline.

title: The diva
summary: The prima donna of the season wants a patron. Invite her to court, send flowers and jewels, or ignore her.

title: Murder in the boxes
summary: A boyar is found dead in his box during the third act, drained white. Investigate (a clever ruler may find the vampire boyars, praag.41), hush it up, or blame the Ungols.

title: The cult in the opera house
summary: Under the stage of the old opera house a Chaos cult meets between performances. Raid it (martial: the cult broken and doom eased a little, but the season is lost), let the Court Chekist break it quietly (intrigue), or close the house for a season and hope.

title: The Z'ra heirs
summary: When the crown of Kislev is weak, the heirs of the old Z'ra rulers come to Praag's lord with Ungol swords behind them. Champion them (stand for independence with the factions; a Z'ra heir joins the court), betray them to the Tzar(ina) (favour, gold, and the duchy of Praag if the crown holds it), or send them away.

summary: A child of the Wastes dreams of Tzeentch and becomes a prophet.

summary: The march scatters.

summary: The child's lord may sponsor the march, send men, feed it, sell the children to the slavers, set guards on them or let them go.

title: A prophet in the Wastes
summary: (ravenchild.7).

summary: Every two months or so the child grows, may gain followers and captains, one ruler of the land being crossed hears of it (ravenchild.10), and after three stops the march moves on (ravenchild_move_effect).

summary: The children ask for food, men, or anger the priests; a child of the court may run off to join them, and the AI sends spare children along. the child (ravenchild.9).

summary: prophet (ravenchild.10).

summary: My  is gone. Swayed by the sermons of , crept out in the night to join the Raven's Child on the march to Kislev.

summary: (ravenchild_move_effect).

summary: (ravenchild_move_effect).

summary: (ravenchild_move_effect).

summary: Kislev fell to Chaos or became the target of a Black Crusade before the children arrived. (ravenchild_move_effect).

title: The war begins (hidden)
summary: The gathered forces become armies, morale becomes a modifier, and the child declares war on the holder of Kislev.

title: Light troops (hidden)
summary: Loops through ravenchild_light_troops_effect until the forces variable is spent.

title: Kislev falls to the children (told to Kislev)
summary: Newly made vassals may bend the knee or be cast out.

title: Kislev falls to the children (told to the Dark Gods)
summary: The sponsor may take up the child's line.

title: The reconquest ends
summary: Clears every reconquest flag and disbands the levies and ships.

title: A promised ally leaves the faith
The moment passes
summary: Two years after the oath and still no war: a player's reconquest lapses, the AI marches on the nearest target.

title: The allies march
summary: The war begins: every lord who promised to join does.

title: A promise is sent
summary: (promise_to_join_reconquista).

title: An ally's promise
summary: When you march to take back the south, my banners will march with yours. Send word, and I will come.Your ally,

title: The call to arms
summary: The hour has come. My host marches against the occupiers, and I hold you to your promise. Bring your swords.

title: The Shield of the South
summary: A defender who throws back the reconquest twice founds a bloodline.

title: The Reconqueror
summary: A reconquistador who wins back two lands of the south founds a bloodline and takes up the reconqueror's helm.

title: A sword for hire
summary: A lord offers to fight in a reconquest war for gold: a faithful lord for the occupiers, or a foreign one for the reconquest. (reconquest_sellsword_for_defender, reconquest_sellsword_for_attacker).

title: The offer is taken
summary: Your terms are accepted. The gold is on its way. See that your swords earn it.

title: The offer is spurned
summary: I would rather lose this war than win it with the help of a sellsword who has no loyalty but to his purse. Keep your swords.

title: Gold for your sword
summary: A side at war offers a lord gold to fight for it. (reconquest_hire_sellsword_defender, reconquest_hire_sellsword_attacker).

title: The lord takes the gold
summary: The gold is received. My swords march to join yours.

title: The lord refuses
summary: I am not a sellsword, whatever you may have heard. Find someone else to bleed for you.

title: The year of preparation
summary: Every month or so while preparing (every few days for an adventurer), one of the preparation events; at the end of the year, reconquest.49.

title: The muster
summary: How much gold to spend on the levies.

title: The temple's purse
summary: The head of the faith offers gold for the war, at a price in piety.

title: A captain of the south
summary: A seasoned captain of Estalia or Tilea offers to lead the host.

title: Ships for the south
summary: Ship-owners and Tilean merchant princes offer their galleys.

title: Ready to march
summary: The year of preparation is over. A player picks the war; an adventurer, or an AI that let two years pass, marches on the nearest occupier.

title: A southern lord swears the oath
summary: Sent to every lord of Estalia and Tilea. (prepare_reconquista).

title: The south is free
summary: No ruler outside the Old World faiths holds land in Estalia or Tilea. reconquest_declare_war_effect).

title: An adventurer of the south
summary: A southern king or emperor at peace, with occupied land in the south and no reconquest under way, may find an adventurer at his court who will lead one for him.

title: An adventurer asks for backing
summary: A young with a fine sword and a finer tongue has come to court. is , an adventurer of blood who has sworn to win back the lands of the south from their foreign...

title: What kind of patron
summary: is preparing to march, and my court is waiting to see what kind of patron I will be. My name, my prayers or my purse: any of them would help the young...

title: On campaign
summary: A player commanding for the reconquest in occupied land may meet the usual adventures of a crusade.

title: The road south
summary: A quarter of battles and sieges won for the reconquest lead to reconquest.70. on_major_battle_won_leader, on_siege_won_leader).

title: AI cooldown
summary: After an AI swears the oath, no AI may do so again for 15 years.

title: Asking to join the Guild
summary: A character asks to join the Guild. The highest-ranked member who is not a prisoner (or the leader, if all are) answers with the welcome letter.

title: Welcome letter ping
summary: Passes the applicant back so the welcome letter comes from the greeter.

title: Welcome to the Clan of Morgrim
summary: The greeter welcomes the applicant into the Guild.

calls: runesmith.141; runesmith.160; runesmith.26; runesmith.30; runesmith.50; runesmith.70
title: Guild quest tombola
summary: Every two years a free member is handed a mission by another member or by his apprentice: a commission for a dwarf lord, an apprentice, a forge, a hunt for lost rune lore, ore and salves, or a raid on a rival's forge. The AI often skips the mission and just gains or loses influence.

title: A forge of my own
summary: From the build_smithy decision. Begin the work or take the coin back.

title: Where to cut the forge
summary: Deep in the hold (hidden), in the forge quarter (better forge, easy to find), or far away in a sea cave or the mountain roots (hidden and roomy).

title: How great a forge
summary: The size of the forge sets how many fittings follow (the ambition) and what it costs. The two biggest need a learned smith or a learned apprentice.

title: The anvil
summary: A runesmith forges his own anvil and never works on another's. A plain iron anvil, or one faced with gromril for more coin.

title: The furnace
summary: A charcoal furnace, or a deep shaft to the mountain's own heat.

title: Hammers and chisels
summary: Tools from the clan smiths, or tools of old make bought from a fallen clan.

title: The rune tablets
summary: The Guild writes no lore down, but the forge needs stone tablets of practice runes and a wall of grudges. Cut them himself, or have a runescribe cut them.

title: The forge is finished
summary: Clears the building flags and picks the finished forge by its level.

title: A humble forge
summary: The forge is finished. It is small and the smoke stings the eyes, and a passing smith from the forge quarter called it a cupboard with a fire in it. But the...

title: A sound forge
summary: The forge is finished: a sound, honest forge, with a good anvil and a fire that draws well. The old smiths who come to look at it nod and say little, which...

title: A fine forge
summary: The forge is finished, and it is a fine one. Two furnaces, an anvil that rings true, a wall for its grudges and room for an apprentice. The clan smiths come to...

title: A great forge
summary: The forge is finished and the whole hold has come to see it. The furnaces stand around the anvil like the six furnaces around Kenaz in Karak Norn, the rune...

title: A forge the ancestors would know
summary: It is done. The furnaces burn on the mountain's own heat, the anvil is faced with gromril, the tools are of old make and the rune tablets were cut by masters....

title: Mishap: the forge fire gets loose
summary: A badly banked fire bursts in the night. A forge deep in the hold burns a courtier too. Ore and salves in store may be lost.

title: Mishap: the other guilds grumble
summary: The jewelsmiths and the clan smiths call the runesmith's forge arrogant and their apprentices pick fights with his. Change the plans or pay in standing.

title: Mishap: a salve spoils
summary: Damp gets into the store and a rune salve spoils.

title: Mission: build a forge
summary: A Guild elder, or the member's own apprentice, says a runesmith without a forge of his own is no runesmith.

title: Mission done: the forge is lit
summary: The forge mission ends; the finer the forge, the more the Guild honours it.

title: Mission: find an apprentice
summary: A runesmith is duty-bound to pass the lore on. If no one is named within half a year, a candidate turns up (runesmith.32).

title: A kinsman with the gift
summary: Still no apprentice: a young kinsman of the master's line with the gift is brought to court. Apprentices are male, as in the sagas.

title: The candidate
summary: Take him on as apprentice, or keep looking.

title: The apron and the oath
summary: The mission ends when the member names anyone apprentice. A learned apprentice earns more.

title: The apprenticeship ends (ping)
summary: Twelve to fifteen years after the apron, if the apprentice still serves his master, the master is told.

title: His own anvil
summary: The apprentice has forged his own anvil and is a runesmith in his own right.

title: The apprentice dies
summary: Tells the master (a player) and stops any ore trip the apprentice was on.

title: Word of the apprentice's death
summary: Grief if the master liked a gifted apprentice, relief otherwise.

title: The master dies
summary: A dead member's apprentices lose their title.

title: Mission ping: rune lore of a fallen hold
Mission: rune lore of a fallen hold

title: Where to search
summary: The mission giver names the places. With luck (better with learning) he also has the way into a lost hold's rune-vault.

title: The search ends (ping)
summary: Sends the member the outcome the dice chose, then clears the flags.

title: The rune-vault of the lost hold
summary: Found: one of the ancestors' master runes the member does not have yet. Once in a lifetime.

title: Rune tablets in the old workings
summary: In the old workings in you find what you came for: a row of rune tablets, half buried in fallen rock, struck by a smith whose mark no one living knows. Some of...

summary: With the priests' leave you lift the slab under the shrine at . Beneath it is a second slab, struck with runes in an older hand, and a rune of warding that has...

title: An old tally in the Guild halls
summary: Weeks in the tally-halls among the counts of runes struck and the names of the smiths who struck them. Most of it is what you knew already. But in the tally of...

title: Kruk: the search comes to nothing
summary: Each place has its own failure. After the lost hold the member suspects the mission giver of a false map and makes him a rival.

title: A rune in the rubble
summary: The old workings hold a finished rune, sealed in its stone. Only for a member with no rune yet, once in a lifetime.

title: Mission ping: raid a rival's forge
Mission: raid a rival's forge
summary: Picks the target and asks the member to join the raid.

title: Find the forge, or go straight in
summary: A hidden forge must be found first (runesmith.73); an open one is reached at once.

title: The accomplice is still looking
summary: The accomplice's spies are hunting for the forge. The deeper it is cut, the longer it takes.

title: The forge-wardens
summary: Bribe the wardens, spike their keg with a rune salve, let the accomplice pick a quarrel at the door, or turn back.

title: Inside the forge
summary: Past the wardens (bought or asleep). Split up or stay together, steal or wreck. If the wardens wake or see through the quarrel, the raiders are caught.

title: The wardens drink it and stay awake
summary: Dwarf heads are hard; the spiked keg does nothing. The raid is off.

title: The quarrel works
summary: The wardens are busy with the accomplice. Steal or wreck, alone.

title: The quarrel fails
summary: The accomplice's insult is so feeble the wardens laugh. The raid is off.

title: Caught
summary: The wardens take the member (and an AI accomplice) to the rival's cells.

title: Thieves in the cells
summary: The rival decides: trade rune secrets for freedom, or let them rot.

title: The offer
summary: The rival offers freedom for rune secrets. Talk, or stay in the cell.

title: The thief talks
summary: talks. Some of it may even be true. You let the thief go.

title: The thief will not talk
summary: will not say a word. At least the thief knows how to keep a secret.

title: Left to rot
summary: has no use for you. You will stay in this cell until someone pays for you, or until you die.

title: The theft
summary: A great haul takes a rune from the rival's rune-chest, a good one a store of ore or salve, a poor one only coin.

title: Robbed
summary: The rival finds the theft. A great or good haul moves the rune and the store to the thief.

title: The wrecking
summary: Total ruin of the forge (the rival loses his forge modifier and his stores), heavy damage, or a rune-ward on the anvil kills the member.

title: The forge is wrecked
summary: The rival finds the damage, or the raider's corpse at the anvil.

title: The accomplice steals
summary: Good haul, poor haul, or caught (runesmith.80 for the member).

title: The accomplice's haul
summary: A good haul gives the member a store of ore.

title: The accomplice wrecks
summary: Damage, or the accomplice dies at the rune-ward.

title: The accomplice's wrecking
summary: comes back covered in soot and grinning. "They will not light that forge again this year."

title: The accomplice dies at the ward
summary: You hear a flash and a scream from inside the forge. has found the rune-ward on the anvil. There is no time to go back for the body.

title: Away clean
summary: The raid is done. Close accomplices may become friends.

title: Change paths
summary: Swaps one path trait for another.

title: The old tablets
summary: Go down to the Guild's tablet-vaults (paying for access once), or learn from the old smiths who still remember.

title: A keeper of the old lore
summary: Months among the tablets, and the old smiths' stories. Runes that were only names to you now have shapes, and you know why the Rule of Three is the Rule of...

title: The hammer and the chant
summary: Learn by striking runes at the anvil, or by sitting with the chants until the shape of each rune is known by heart.

title: A master of the hammer and the chant
summary: A season of it, from the first bell to the last. When you strike a rune now, you no longer think about it. You hear it ring before the hammer falls.

title: The ancestors
summary: Keep vigil at Valaya's hearth (diplomacy) or swear an oath at Grimnir's shrine (martial).

title: Close to the ancestors
summary: You come back from the shrine changed. The ancestors were close, closer than they have been in years, and you think they were pleased with you.

title: Call a Runemoot
summary: It has been a long time since the runesmiths of the Guild worked together at one forge. A Runemoot: a gathering of masters, each with their own lore, to strike...

title: The guests are chosen
summary: A friend or a famous smith as guest of honour, a second guest, and either two more or a guest who brings someone the host dislikes.

title: Bring my friend
summary: The third guest asks the host to invite someone the host dislikes. Turning him away (or both) is a scandal.

title: What shall we forge?
summary: The host proposes a work of war, of the hold's wealth, or of lore. A guest may object (runesmith.115) or all may agree (runesmith.117).

title: A guest objects
summary: The guest wants a different work. Argue it out, give way, or overrule him as host (a scandal).

title: All agree
summary: No one objects. For once, a room full of runesmiths agrees on something. It may be the ale.

title: The host wins the argument
summary: The Rorkaz goes on until the lamps burn low. At last runs out of breath and sits down, red in the face. You have won.

title: The host loses the argument
summary: The guest's work is forged instead, and the host loses face.

title: The old way or the new
summary: Two guests split over the work: the first wants to try something no smith has struck before, the second to keep to the runes the ancestors taught. Then a quarrel, a friendship or a flash of insight may follow.

title: Two guests quarrel
summary: Make peace between them, or send one home (a scandal).

title: Peace is made
summary: You get them to sit down, and to drink, and in the end to shake hands. They will not be friends. But they will work.

title: Peace fails
summary: The quarrel gets worse and the moot slides into a major scandal.

title: Two hammers in time
summary: The host and a guest work well together and may become friends.

title: The rune in the night
summary: Alone at the anvil, the host sees how the work must go.

title: The outcome
summary: Adds up the guests' learning and rolls the result. The bold road can reach the best work but can also end in disaster.

title: The work is done
summary: Nine results by work and success. Artifacts go only to a host who does not already own that one; techpoints and Guild standing always.

title: The work fails
summary: Nothing comes of the safe road; the bold one can end in a blast that maims or kills host and guests.

title: Scandal
summary: A first scandal is minor, a second major, a third ends the moot.

title: The guests walk out
summary: The moot ends with nothing forged.

title: Ore and salves
summary: Pick a companion, then mine or trade.

title: Mission: ore and salves
summary: has been through your store and does not like what found. "Half your salve has gone to crust and there is more rust than ore in here. Get yourself fresh stock,...

summary: How the two of them go about it depends on their stewardship.

title: What the workings gave up
summary: Rune salves for every good seam. Nothing found can mean a fall of rock.

title: To the traders' halls
summary: How the two of them haggle depends on their diplomacy.

title: What the traders sold
summary: Metals for every fair bargain, paid for in gold.

title: Gathering clean-up
summary: Clears the trip if it stalls (a companion died on the way).

title: Mission: a commission
summary: Picks a client: a dwarf lord of the realm, else one of a neighbour's. The AI works it off on its own (runesmith.167).

title: The year runs out
summary: A letter from the Guild:"A year has passed, and has delivered nothing. The Guild's word was given, and has broken it. This will be remembered."

title: The client's wish
summary: The client wants a weapon, armour, or (from a member of rank 2 or more) a rune. Weapons and armour take a metal, a rune a salve; gromril makes a masterwork. A lord who already has a weapon is less likely to want one.

title: At the anvil
summary: A decent piece, or a long labour that may become a masterwork.

title: The work is done
summary: Deliver it to the client, or keep it. Theft costs Guild standing and prestige, and a thief of little standing is cast out or demoted.

title: A school of rune lore

title: The stanitsa refuses
summary: The mission fails; the stanitsa is angry for years.

title: The stanitsa turns
summary: The mission succeeds: the stanitsa keeps Ursun, Dazh and Tor now.

title: The last stand
summary: Ungol raiders fall on a Ropsmann camp. Stand with the pikes (a fight the Ropsmann know how to win), fall back into the woods (the camp burns), or pay them off.

title: Furs and amber
summary: Gospodar merchants come for the Ropsmann's furs and amber. Sell to them (a few years of good trade), take the amber to Erengrad yourself, or keep outsiders away from the camps.

title: One people, or our own

title: The keeper of the tongue
summary: Rarely, an old keeper of the Ropsmann tongue, the speech Kislevarin came from, comes to a court with Ropsmann lands. Take them in (learning at court; the court's Ropsmann hold out against the melting pot; one time in ten a birch-bark chronicle), or send them away.

title: The Geheimnisnacht Ball

title: An invitation to Drakenhof

title: The ball is over
summary: Vlad, a player, hears how the night went.

summary: The lord chooses what to bind: a weapon or a suit of armour. The result follows at once (undead.52).

title: The binding
summary: A Necrarch never fails. A necromancer of the realm fails one time in ten, the lord himself one time in seven: the item survives, but the spell is lost. On success the item becomes a necromantic one of its kind (undead_enchant_weapon_effect, undead_enchant_armour_effect).

summary: The employer learns that the mercenary turned and took one of the court.
